transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I haven’t really been sleeping much since the warehouse inspection. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I keep lying there replaying parts of what happened, and if I do fall asleep I wake up sweaty and completely awake… like I’m back near that blast. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing I should come in for, but it’s been getting hard to manage.
Have you been avoiding anything that reminds you of the warehouse inspection?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still trying to keep up with work, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just refusing everything. But I’ve been kind of avoiding the warehouse file, and when calls come in about industrial accounts I’ve been letting them go to voicemail. Even opening those emails makes my stomach drop. I know that probably isn’t ideal.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the warehouse inspection, like it's happening all over again?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I literally think I’m back there every time, but during the day I’ll be reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and all of a sudden I get this really sharp image of the worker on the floor, and the soot in the air. And my body just reacts before I can really talk myself out of it.

I don’t know if that counts as “reliving it,” but it feels… pretty immediate when it happens.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since the warehouse inspection?

It’s been about a week now… basically since the warehouse inspection, the one where the explosion happened. I kept thinking it would settle down after a couple days, so I didn’t want to overreact, but it hasn’t really gone away yet.
Are there any people, places, or activities that you're avoiding because they remind you of the warehouse inspection?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m avoiding everything, exactly. I’m still doing my job. But I have been sort of… putting off the warehouse file, and when calls come in about industrial accounts, I’ve been letting them go to voicemail more than I should.

Even opening those emails makes my stomach drop a little. I know that probably sounds not great, but I’m trying to keep up.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most of the time since the warehouse inspection?

Yeah… I mean, I’m trying not to make too much of it, but I do feel pretty jumpy. Like if the printer jams, or a door slams, or someone comes up behind my desk, I kind of… react before I can stop myself. I jump like something awful is happening.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I usually settle down after a few minutes, but it takes longer than it should. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel like you're detached from yourself or the world around you, like you're in a fog or observing things from outside your body?

I don’t think so… not like outside my body, anyway. Sometimes I’m a little spacey, but I think that might just be from being tired or distracted. I haven’t really noticed feeling like the world isn’t real or anything like that.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you avoided talking to anyone about the warehouse inspection?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m not trying to shut people out or be difficult… I just haven’t really wanted to get into it much.

At work especially, I’ve been more avoiding the warehouse file itself and letting calls about industrial accounts go to voicemail, because even seeing those emails come in makes my stomach drop. So if someone brings it up, I tend to keep it brief or say I’ll look at it later.

I know that’s probably not the best way to handle it.
Have you avoided social activities or interactions with friends and family since the warehouse inspection?

Not really with friends or family, I don’t think. I mean, I’ve maybe been a little quieter, but I’m still answering people and doing the usual stuff.

The main thing I’ve been avoiding is more work-related… the warehouse file, and calls about industrial accounts. I’ve let some of those go to voicemail because even opening those emails makes my stomach drop. I know that’s not exactly what you asked, but that’s the part I’ve noticed most.
Have you avoided places or situations that remind you of the warehouse inspection to the point where it's significantly impacted your daily life or relationships?

I wouldn’t say it’s affected my relationships, exactly… I don’t think anyone’s upset with me or anything. But daily life at work, yes, a bit.

I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file, and I’ve let calls about industrial accounts go to voicemail because even seeing those emails or opening them makes my stomach drop. I know that probably sounds like I’m making it worse by putting it off, but I just… have a hard time making myself deal with it.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened during the warehouse inspection?

I’m not sure. I mean… I don’t think I did anything wrong, exactly. At least, I keep telling myself that.

But I do catch myself wondering if I should’ve handled something differently, or noticed something sooner. I don’t know if that counts as feeling responsible. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.
Have you avoided anything else related to the warehouse inspection besides the file and calls about industrial accounts?

Not really anything else that I can think of… I mean, it’s mostly been that same work stuff.

The warehouse file, and the industrial account calls. I’ve let some of them go to voicemail, and I put off opening those emails because I get this drop in my stomach when I see them. But I don’t think I’ve been avoiding other parts of my life, if that makes sense.
Have you stopped doing anything important to you because it reminds you of the warehouse inspection?

I don’t think I’ve stopped anything important-important, if that makes sense. It’s more… at work, I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file and letting the industrial account calls go to voicemail.

Even just opening those emails makes my stomach drop, so I put it off. I know that’s not great, but I’m not trying to avoid everything—just that stuff, really.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy since the warehouse inspection?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway. I mean, I haven’t really noticed myself not caring about things I usually like.

Maybe I’ve been a little distracted, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest. Does that answer it okay?
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not in a situation that would normally be considered dangerous?

I don’t think so… I mean, not constantly. I haven’t really noticed myself scanning for danger or anything like that when I’m just out doing normal things.

Maybe I’m a little more on edge sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m on the lookout for threats. I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed yourself pulling away from or having less interest in hobbies or activities that you usually find enjoyable?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ve still been doing the normal things I like when I have time. Maybe I’m not as focused or I get tired sooner, but I wouldn’t say I’m pulling away from hobbies or not enjoying them.

I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean.
How long have you been avoiding the warehouse file and industrial account calls?

Um… probably about a week now. Since the warehouse inspection, the one where the explosion happened.

I mean, I haven’t been avoiding everything, exactly, but the file and those account calls… yeah, I’ve been putting those off since then. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Have you avoided the warehouse or any similar places since the inspection?

I haven’t gone back to the warehouse, no. I guess I’ve been kind of avoiding anything connected to it more than the place itself… like the warehouse file, and I’ve been letting calls about industrial accounts go to voicemail.

It sounds silly, but even opening the emails makes my stomach drop a little, so I just… don’t. Or I tell myself I’ll do it later. Is that what you mean by avoiding?
